drills.q: Compute required n per arm: baseline 5%, detect +10% relative, alpha .05, power .8.
You have 12,000 users/arm and a 5% baseline. What relative MDE can you detect at 80% power?
drills.a: delta = (1.96+0.84) x sqrt(2 x 0.05 x 0.95 / 12000) ~= 0.0158 absolute -> ~31.6% relative MDE. If your plausible lift is +10%, this test is underpowered - don't run it and call the null 'no effect'.

drills.q: Stakeholder wants results by Friday; you get 8K eligible users/day. Respond with numbers.
drills.a: By Friday (~4-5 days) you collect ~32-40K total (~16-20K/arm), buying roughly +-1.9-2.2pt absolute noise floor on a 5% baseline (~38-44% relative MDE) - far above any plausible effect. Show that MDE-vs-deadline table and renegotiate: two weeks buys ~+10% relative.

drills.q: Design the sequential-testing setup for an exec who WILL check daily.
drills.a: Either group-sequential alpha spending with pre-declared looks (day-3/7/14 boundaries where early looks need extreme z-scores like |z|>3+), or anytime-valid mSPRT p-values valid under arbitrary stopping. Policy fix too: dashboard shows sequential-valid stats or hides significance until planned end.

drills.q: Week-1 read shows +18% engagement; week-3 steady state is +7%. Ship decision math?
drills.a: Price against STEADY state (+7%), not peak: maintenance + inference COGS recur monthly, so halving effects often flip NPV negative. Check where the win concentrated (segments), then decide; also note monotone decay predicted shrinkage - the trajectory was the tell.

drills.q: An AI feature costs $60K/mo inference at full rollout. Sketch the experiment plan.
drills.a: Compute break-even uplift first (what gain covers $60K/mo), power the test against THAT as minimum interesting effect; add cost guardrails (tokens/session cap, cost/session target); consider staged rollout to bound learning spend; write the dollar kill-threshold before launch.

drills.q: Referral feature test shows no lift under user-level randomization. What might be wrong?
drills.a: Interference: treated users' referrals change control users' outcomes, diluting estimates toward zero and hiding real network value. Fix: cluster randomization by graph community or geo so spillover stays within arms, accepting higher variance/fewer effective units.

drills.q: 15 concurrent experiments across teams - what infrastructure discipline is mandatory?
drills.a: Layered orthogonal hashing so tests share traffic without colliding; central assignment service with consistent unit IDs; automated SRM/guardrail gates on every dashboard; multiple-comparison policy; decision log linking launches to readouts. Same-surface tests need exclusive layers or explicit factorial interaction analysis.

drills.q: Traffic is 2,000 users/week. Can anything meaningful be A/B tested? Options?
drills.a: At ~4K total over two weeks the detectable relative MDE on a 10% baseline exceeds ~40% - nothing product-relevant fits. Switch instruments: interrupted time series, day-level switchbacks, synthetic control, moderated-test proxy outcomes; or fix traffic itself as the binding constraint on future learning.

drills.q: A teammate proposes dropping confidence from 95% to 80% to ship faster. Legitimate?
drills.a: Legitimate IF pre-declared and priced: consciously accepting more false positives for speed/power. Illegitimate when done post-hoc to make a marginal result significant - that's peeking with extra steps. Write the error-budget tradeoff into the plan before results exist.
